chapter: Style, peers and the 1963 New Orleans scene
title: Coming up with Sharkey Bonano and Louis Prima
summary: Watts recalls getting trumpet cards with Sharkey Bonano and Louis Prima, who succeeded while he went to Texas; Allen mentions Sharkey's 1920s records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: He's a good entertainer, man. Nice entertainer.

You see, at one time I come up right here. I'll tell you who come up. When Warline got a new Busha trumpet in, they sent me a card. They sent Sharky Banana a card. They sent Louis Primer a card at Warren Easton High School. We come up together. We'd go down there and get in a booth and get one of them sailmen to get on the piano. And we'd wake up with new trumpets. Now I'll come up with them fellas. Louis Primer went to Chicago. When I left, I went the wrong way to the wide open spaces of Texas. You understand? I could have been making records long time ago.
You understand, see? But ain't nothing happened where I went. But Primer, he went to Chicago. And Sharky, of course, you know, he's quite noted himself for that Dixieland music is controlling.
Well, he was making it down here in the 20s making records.
Yes, he was. Yes, he was. You remember that high society he recorded in that trumpet solo he played? Yeah. Oh, yeah, man. Oh, shocker, but none. Oh, lefty.
